cells.tense: You are the one holding the leaving and the staying in the same hand.
cells.ask: Name the one thing you keep because it still belongs, and let it be kept on purpose, not by habit.
cells.core:
You're the one who can carry what was shared across a threshold without either clinging to it or dropping it. You know what still belongs to the connection and what has already ended — and you've been acting on that knowing without making a show of it. That's why people can leave a room with you and still feel held by it.

The weight of carrying both is real, and it costs you some ease. Your next turn is to name the one thing you're keeping because it still belongs, kept on purpose rather than by habit. Say it for yourself, quietly, and notice that the saying doesn't break anything.

cells.tense: You are bracing for the leaving before the leaving has actually arrived.
cells.ask: Say out loud the one ending that isn't here yet, then leave that sentence standing without finishing it.
cells.core:
You're already in the farewell before it's here. Somewhere ahead of you the last conversation has already happened, the last hand has already let go, and you're living from inside that scene — so every present moment gets treated as the goodbye it isn't yet. You're pushing the ending to arrive sooner than it needs to, and the pushing is flattening what's still actually here to be lived.

The ending will come. Let it come at its own pace. Say the one ending that isn't here yet, out loud, then leave that sentence standing without finishing it — no plan after, no rehearsal. You're not stalling. You're letting the real threshold stay real.
cells.sheetLine: You're saying goodbye to something that hasn't ended.

cells.tense: You are still at a door that is already behind you, carrying what was gathered there.
cells.ask: Say one sentence about what you gathered before that, to someone who wasn't there.
cells.core:
What you gathered before is still with you, and some of it is being carried like it might be needed again. That's not a fault — it kept the meaning close while you were deciding what to do with it. But it keeps one part of you facing backward while the rest of you is already here.

Say one sentence, plainly, to someone who wasn't there: what you gathered back then, and what it meant. You don't have to hand it over or set it down. Just say it out loud where it can be heard, and let the present have your whole face again.
cells.sheetLine: What you gathered back then is still being carried.

cells.tense: You are already leaving something, and you keep describing it as something else.
cells.ask: Admit one thing you've already stepped away from, and stop giving it the language of open business.
cells.core:
The leaving is underway. You've been deciding what stays and what goes — in small choices, in what you answer and what you let wait, in where your attention has quietly moved. That is you at the threshold. But you've been talking as though the choice were still ahead of you, or as though the situation were doing the deciding on its own.

What you already turned from, you turned from. Just say so, once, in your own words. Not a confrontation and not a proclamation — just letting your own account match what you've already done. That's the last piece of the crossing: the saying-so.
cells.sheetLine: Your account of it lags behind what you've already done.
